en.Oben der Querschnitt des Flussbetts beim: Top: cross section of the river bed at the station's gauge with the water level at three discharges. Bottom: the mean velocity derived from it: each dot is an hourly value of the last year (discharge ÷ wetted area), the line is the rating curve v̄ = a · Q
en.– Hochwasser des letzten Jahres: höchste: – High water of the last year: highest discharge in the hourly values (higher in only 0.1 % of hours).
en.– Niedrigwasser des letzten Jahres: nur: – Low water of the last year: discharge was lower in only 5 % of hours.
en.Die weisse Linie ist die Flusssohle. All: The white line is the river bed. Everything below a water level is under water at that discharge (wetted area); the areas overlap. The more discharge has to pass through the same area, the faster the water flows: mean velocity = discharge ÷ wetted area.
en.– mittlere Geschwindigkeit je Stunde des: – mean velocity per hour of the last year (discharge ÷ wetted area, sample).
en.– aktueller Abfluss und Geschwindigkeit: – current discharge and velocity from the rating curve.

Factor = velocity in the section relative to the station (impounded 0.33, sills 0.75, free 0.8, narrows 1). Extra margin = surcharge on the upper limit of the drift range, because the main current in the middle of the river is faster than the average; empty = default ({0} %).

Flow velocity and search area remain unchanged.
